```{r}
#| label: setup
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(knitr); library(targets) })
options(knitr.table.format = "html")
root <- ".."                                   # rjkdc-analysis/
repo <- "https://github.com/fhoces/opa-prop40/blob/main/rjkdc-analysis/"
scroll <- function(x) cat("\n\n```{=html}\n<div class=\"table-scroll\">\n",
                          as.character(x), "\n</div>\n```\n\n", sep = "")
link <- function(path) sprintf('<a href="%s%s"><code>%s</code></a>', repo, path, path)
# first comment line of a source file, as its one-line description
describe <- function(path) {
  l <- readLines(file.path(root, path), warn = FALSE)
  if (grepl("[.]py$", path)) {                 # module docstring
    m <- regmatches(paste(l, collapse = " "), regexpr('"""(.*?)"""', paste(l, collapse = " "), perl = TRUE))
    if (!length(m)) return("")
    l <- gsub('"""', "", m)
  } else {                                     # leading comment block
    l <- l[seq_len(which(!grepl("^#", l) | l == "")[1] - 1)]
    l <- sub("^#+ ?", "", l)
  }
  txt <- trimws(paste(trimws(l[!grepl("^!", l)]), collapse = " "))
  if (!nzchar(txt) && path == "_targets.R") return("The pipeline definition: every target below, in one list.")
  out <- sub("^(.*?[.])( .*)?$", "\\1", txt, perl = TRUE)   # first sentence
  if (nchar(out) > 220) paste0(substr(out, 1, 220), "...") else out
}
ts <- read.csv("data/test-summary.csv")
```

::: {.report-intro}
![](assets/opa/opa-materials.png){.opa-figure}

This page is the **Open Materials** layer: everything needed to rebuild every number on this
site, in the repository [github.com/fhoces/opa-prop40](https://github.com/fhoces/opa-prop40/tree/main/rjkdc-analysis),
folder `rjkdc-analysis/`. The analysis is an R [`{targets}`](https://docs.ropensci.org/targets/)
pipeline with a Python twin; the site's explorer grid, report and deck read that pipeline's store and
exports, so none of them retypes a number.
:::

## How to rebuild

```sh
git clone https://github.com/bjaros20/wealth_tax && git -C wealth_tax checkout 25e84dd   # the authors' MIT repo
cd rjkdc-analysis
export RAUH_REPO_DIR=/absolute/path/to/wealth_tax
Rscript -e 'targets::tar_make()'        # pipeline, export/r/*.csv, site/data/*.csv, site/explorer/grid.js
Rscript tests/testthat.R                # the test suite (console summary)
Rscript tests/count_tests.R             # the same suite, counted: site/data/test-summary.csv
/opt/anaconda3/bin/python3 py/run_export.py     # the Python twin: export/py/*.csv
quarto render site/repro.qmd && quarto render site/materials.qmd
Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("site/slides/slides.Rmd")'
```

`RAUH_REPO_DIR` is the single place that knows where the authors' repository lives
(`R/rauh_repo.R`, `py/rauh_repo.py`). Tests that re-run the authors' own scripts skip cleanly
without it; everything else runs.

## Scripts

```{r}
#| results: asis
f <- c(file.path("R", list.files(file.path(root, "R"), pattern = "[.]R$")),
       file.path("py", list.files(file.path(root, "py"), pattern = "[.]py$")),
       "_targets.R", "tests/testthat.R", "tests/count_tests.R")
scroll(kable(data.frame(file = vapply(f, link, ""), `what it does` = vapply(f, describe, ""),
                        check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL), escape = FALSE,
             caption = "R pipeline (R/), Python twin (py/), and the runners"))
```

The pipeline's targets (`tar_manifest()`):

```{r}
#| results: asis
m <- tar_manifest(script = file.path(root, "_targets.R"), fields = c("name", "command"),
                  callr_function = NULL)
m$command <- substr(gsub("\\s+", " ", m$command), 1, 90)
scroll(kable(m, col.names = c("target", "command (first 90 characters)")))
```

## Tests

```{r}
#| results: asis
tot <- colSums(ts[, c("tests", "expectations", "passed", "failed", "skipped")])
scroll(kable(rbind(ts[, c("file", "tests", "expectations", "passed", "failed", "skipped")],
                   data.frame(file = "total", t(tot))), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Counted with testthat's ListReporter by tests/count_tests.R"))
```

**`r tot["tests"]` tests (`r tot["expectations"]` expectations): `r tot["passed"]` passed,
`r tot["failed"]` failed, `r tot["skipped"]` skipped**, run on `r ts$run_date[1]` with R
`r ts$r_version[1]`, with the authors' repository
`r if (all(ts$authors_repo_available)) "available" else "not available (the vs-authors'-script tests skip)"`.
They come in four kinds:

1. **Against the paper's printed number**, at printed rounding for deterministic figures, or within
   four Monte Carlo standard errors for simulated ones.
2. **Against the authors' own scripts**, run unmodified from a scratch copy (plot and CSV paths
   redirected, no logic changed; `tests/testthat/helper-author-scripts.R`).
3. **Parity between the R and Python exports** (`test-parity.R`): deterministic steps to 1e-6,
   Monte Carlo steps within a documented tolerance (numpy cannot share R's random stream).
4. **The site** (`test-site.R`): the explorer's `grid.js` and `site/data/headlines.csv` must be
   byte-identical to the exporter's output; grid cells must equal the pipeline's analytic means and
   brute-force Monte Carlo; the printed-value transcription must agree with the pipeline; every
   number typed into the landing page must still match its source.

A continuous-integration workflow for this folder is configured to rebuild the pipeline and run the suite on each push that touches it
(`.github/workflows/rjkdc-ci.yml`, cloning the authors' repository at the pinned commit).

## CSVs

```{r}
#| results: asis
csvs <- c(file.path("export/r", list.files(file.path(root, "export/r"), pattern = "[.]csv$")),
          file.path("export/py", list.files(file.path(root, "export/py"), pattern = "[.]csv$")),
          file.path("site/data", list.files("data", pattern = "[.]csv$")),
          "DATA-SOURCES.csv")
what <- c("export/r/inputs.csv" = "every input: value, OPA label (data / research / guesswork / scenario / derived), source, page",
          "export/r/outputs.csv" = "every headline figure: reproduced value, printed value, page, absolute difference",
          "export/py/inputs.csv" = "the Python twin's inputs (same schema)",
          "export/py/outputs.csv" = "the Python twin's outputs (same schema)",
          "site/data/headlines.csv" = "the two preferred estimates: printed, reproduced, exact (target site_headlines)",
          "site/data/printed-tables.csv" = "hand transcription of printed Tables 8, 9, 10 and NBER Table 10, with PDF pages (checked by test-site.R)",
          "site/data/test-summary.csv" = "test counts per file (tests/count_tests.R)",
          "DATA-SOURCES.csv" = "the source manifest (below)")
rows <- vapply(csvs, function(p) nrow(read.csv(file.path(root, p))), 0)
scroll(kable(data.frame(file = vapply(csvs, link, ""), rows = rows, contents = unname(what[csvs]),
                        row.names = NULL), escape = FALSE))
```

The explorer's grid, `site/explorer/grid.js`, is also generated (target `site_grid_js`): 2,187 cells,
never edited by hand.

## Sources {#sources}

None of these files is committed; each is listed with where it came from and its SHA-256 hash.
The papers are not redistributed; the authors' repository is MIT licensed and read from a local
clone.

```{r}
#| results: asis
ds <- read.csv(file.path(root, "DATA-SOURCES.csv"))
ds$sha256 <- paste0("<code>", substr(ds$sha256, 1, 16), "&hellip;</code>")
ds$url_or_contact <- sprintf('<a href="%s">link</a>', ds$url_or_contact)
ds$feeds <- ifelse(nchar(ds$feeds) > 160, paste0(substr(ds$feeds, 1, 160), "&hellip;"), ds$feeds)
scroll(kable(ds[, c("file", "provider", "obtained_via", "date_obtained", "url_or_contact", "sha256", "terms", "feeds")],
             escape = FALSE, row.names = FALSE))
```

## The nine mismatches {#mismatches}

```{r}
#| results: asis
mm <- readLines(file.path(root, "MISMATCHES.md"))
mm <- mm[-seq_len(which(grepl("^# ", mm))[1])]      # drop the file's own title
mm <- sub("^## ", "### ", mm)
cat(mm, sep = "\n")
```
